claims.claim: Hobb says that in a short story she cuts everything that does not describe the setting, advance the plot or give a character insight.
claims.source: Robin Hobb, interviewed by Other Fantasy (OF Blog, Larry Nolen), 2003
claims.quote: cut out everything that does not describe the setting

claims.claim: Hobb states that her prose written as Megan Lindholm is much leaner than her prose written as Robin Hobb.
claims.source: Robin Hobb, interviewed by Other Fantasy (OF Blog, Larry Nolen), 2003
claims.quote: Prose as Megan Lindholm is much leaner than prose as Robin Hobb

claims.claim: Hobb says that in a novel she sprawls, and knows she does.
claims.source: Robin Hobb, interviewed by Other Fantasy (OF Blog, Larry Nolen), 2003
claims.quote: In a novel, I sprawl, and I know it

claims.claim: Hobb tells aspiring writers to make the economy and geography of an invented place make sense.
claims.source: Robin Hobb, interviewed by Other Fantasy (OF Blog, Larry Nolen), 2003
claims.quote: Make your economy and geography make sense

claims.claim: Hobb gives as an error of scale the idea that a tiny village would support an artisan who specialises in doorknockers.
claims.source: Robin Hobb, interviewed by Other Fantasy (OF Blog, Larry Nolen), 2003
claims.quote: A tiny village isn't going to have an artisan

claims.claim: Hobb gives as an error of labour scale the idea that a medieval farm family harvested its entire farm in one afternoon.
claims.source: Robin Hobb, interviewed by Other Fantasy (OF Blog, Larry Nolen), 2003
claims.quote: A medieval farm family didn't harvest its entire farm in one afternoon

claims.claim: Hobb says every character, however small the part, is the main character while on stage.
claims.source: Robin Hobb, interviewed by Other Fantasy (OF Blog, Larry Nolen), 2003
claims.quote: Every character is the main character

claims.claim: Hobb says that inside a villain's skin the villain is wondering what is for dinner tonight.
claims.source: Robin Hobb, interviewed by Other Fantasy (OF Blog, Larry Nolen), 2003
claims.quote: even the villain is wondering what is for dinner tonight

claims.claim: Hobb names immediacy and reader identification as the benefits she found in writing Farseer in first person.
claims.source: Robin Hobb, interviewed by Other Fantasy (OF Blog, Larry Nolen), 2003

claims.claim: Hobb says first person confined her to telling the reader only what Fitz knew at that moment.
claims.source: Robin Hobb, interviewed by Other Fantasy (OF Blog, Larry Nolen), 2003
claims.quote: I could only tell the reader what Fitz knew at that moment

claims.claim: Hobb calls the first person voice the natural voice for the story teller.
claims.source: Robin Hobb, interviewed by Aidan Moher, A Dribble of Ink, 2007
claims.quote: the first person voice is the natural voice for the story teller

claims.claim: Hobb says first person makes the reader privy to the viewpoint character's innermost thoughts and feelings.
claims.source: Robin Hobb, interviewed by Aidan Moher, A Dribble of Ink, 2007
claims.quote: the reader is privy to the characters innermost thoughts and feelings

claims.claim: Hobb says that writing as Hobb she tends to write longer, more detailed stories.
claims.source: Robin Hobb, interviewed by Aidan Moher, A Dribble of Ink, 2007
claims.quote: I tend to write longer, more detailed stories
claims.page: Q on the two pen names

claims.claim: Hobb says the Lindholm writing style is not as leisurely as the Hobb style.
claims.source: Robin Hobb, interviewed by Aidan Moher, A Dribble of Ink, 2007
claims.quote: The Lindholm writing style is not as leisurely
claims.page: Q on the two pen names

claims.claim: Hobb says that when her characters are hurt they acquire baggage that may later affect what they do.
claims.source: Robin Hobb, interviewed by Aidan Moher, A Dribble of Ink, 2007
claims.quote: they acquire baggage and later on it may affect what they do
